title: Rowan Bell · Community Manager · call with Gilda Fernham · January 2024
notice: Synthetic demo material. Invented document; no real meeting, publication, email or call occurred.

blocks.text: Rowan Bell checking in. Gilda sounded busy but cheerful.

Oh, it’s been a good start to the year. You remember the bakery two streets over, the one with the sourdough? We got to talking before the holidays about how we were both making runs to the same three cafes at the crack of dawn. So we tried combining them. Now their van picks up my flower buckets for the Lattices, the Corner Cup, and the Bramble Cafe on Tuesdays and Fridays. Saves me a trip, gets the pastries and the flowers there before the breakfast rush—it just makes sense.
Rowan noted the efficiency and asked if there were any challenges.

Just a bit of coordination, but it’s smoothing out. The drivers know the drill now. On a completely different note, something sweet happened last week. A neighbor from Meadow Mutual Aid stopped in and mentioned she’d heard about a wedding bouquet disaster—the one coming in from Quadling got crushed on the Brickway coach. The bride was in a state. So I just pulled some peonies and ranunculus from my display coolers, added some silvery greens, and tied it up. Had it ready before the ceremony started. It wasn’t the planned bouquet, but she said it was perfect.
Rowan expressed admiration for the quick thinking. Gilda downplayed it.
It’s just flowers. You can’t have a bride without a bouquet. It worked out.
